abstract: MODBUS is an application-layer (OSI level 7) request/reply messaging protocol that provides client/server communication between devices connected on different types of buses or networks. It has been the industry's serial de-facto standard since 1979 and continues to enable millions of automation devices to communicate. The Internet community can access MODBUS at the reserved system port 502 on the TCP/IP stack. The protocol defines a simple Protocol Data Unit (PDU) independent of the underlying communication layers; the mapping on specific buses or networks introduces some additional fields on the Application Data Unit (ADU) — server address (1 B) + CRC (2 B) for RTU on RS-232/RS-485, ':' + 2-ASCII address + LRC + CR-LF for ASCII on serial, or a 7-byte MBAP Header (Transaction ID + Protocol ID + Length + Unit ID) for MODBUS TCP. The application protocol itself is defined by function codes — 1 byte each (range 1..255 decimal; 128..255 reserved for exception responses, i.e. function code | 0x80; code 0 is invalid). Public function codes cover four broad areas: Bit-Access read/write to Coils and Discrete Inputs, 16-bit-Access read/write to Holding and Input Registers, File Record access, and Diagnostics / Encapsulated Interface Transport.
external_pins: MODBUS is an application-layer protocol, not a chip; it has no physical pinout.
The underlying transport supplies the physical wires:
Modbus RTU/ASCII on EIA/TIA-485 — A (D+) and B (D-) differential pair, optional ground, half-duplex;
Modbus RTU/ASCII on EIA/TIA-232 — TXD, RXD, GND, and optional RTS/CTS/DSR/DTR/DCD/RI handshake;
Modbus TCP — Ethernet (MAC + PHY), MODBUS server reserved at TCP port 502.
package: Not applicable — MODBUS is a protocol specification, distributed as a PDF document (50 pages) by Modbus.org. The 'package' is the OSI-layer-7 application-protocol payload that rides on top of a vendor- and transport-chosen physical layer.

supported_transports.name: Modbus RTU (serial)
supported_transports.duplex: half-duplex on RS-485 / full-duplex on RS-232
supported_transports.adu_format: Address (1 B) + PDU (≤ 253 B) + CRC-16-Modbus (2 B)
supported_transports.framing: End-of-frame = ≥ 3.5 character times of silent line

supported_transports.name: Modbus ASCII (serial)
supported_transports.duplex: half-duplex on RS-485 / full-duplex on RS-232
supported_transports.adu_size_bytes: ≤ 513 characters on the wire (each PDU byte → 2 ASCII hex chars)
supported_transports.adu_format: ':' (0x3A) + Address (2 ASCII hex chars) + PDU as ASCII hex (2N chars) + LRC (2 ASCII hex chars) + CR (0x0D) + LF (0x0A)

supported_transports.name: Modbus TCP
supported_transports.physical_layer: TCP/IP on Ethernet (IEEE 802.3), reserved server port 502
supported_transports.adu_format: MBAP Header (7 B: Transaction ID 2 B + Protocol ID 2 B = 0x0000 + Length 2 B + Unit ID 1 B) + PDU (≤ 253 B)

modes_of_operation.name: Modbus RTU on serial
modes_of_operation.description: Binary 8-bit transmission. Address (1 B) + PDU + CRC-16. End-of-frame = 3.5 character-time silence. Compact and efficient; default for industrial RS-485 multi-drop.

modes_of_operation.name: Modbus ASCII on serial
modes_of_operation.description: ASCII-hex transmission. ':' + 2-ASCII-hex address + 2N ASCII-hex PDU + 2-ASCII-hex LRC + CR LF. Each byte takes 2 chars; ~50% efficiency penalty vs RTU but human-readable and tolerant of large inter-character gaps.

modes_of_operation.name: Modbus TCP (Open MODBUS)
modes_of_operation.description: Binary PDU prefixed with a 7-byte MBAP header. Runs on TCP port 502. No CRC (TCP/IP provides integrity). Transaction ID lets the client correlate multiple concurrent outstanding requests.

modes_of_operation.name: Modbus PLUS (legacy)
modes_of_operation.description: High-speed token-passing peer-to-peer network on HDLC carrier; Modicon-proprietary; deprecated in favor of Modbus TCP.

key_features: Application-layer request/reply protocol — OSI level 7 — independent of the underlying communication layer.
Single-master / multi-slave (legacy serial RTU/ASCII) or client/server (modern TCP) — only one master/client may initiate transactions; servers reply to addressed requests.

Compact 1-byte function code identifies the action requested. Valid range 1..255; 128..255 reserved for exception responses; 0 is invalid; 65..72 and 100..110 are User-Defined ranges; 1..64, 73..99 and 111..127 are Public ranges.

Function-code categories: Bit-Access (read/write Coils + read Discrete Inputs), 16-bit-Access (read/write Holding Registers + read Input Registers), File Record access, and Diagnostics + Encapsulated Interface Transport.
Four primary data tables: Discrete Inputs (1 bit, RO), Coils (1 bit, R/W), Input Registers (16 bit, RO), Holding Registers (16 bit, R/W). Each table addresses up to 65536 items.

Address space: PDU addresses each item 0..65535 (16-bit), while the user-facing data model numbers items 1..n; the spec explicitly states 'a MODBUS data numbered X is addressed in the MODBUS PDU X-1'.
Big-Endian byte order on the wire: a 16-bit value 0x1234 transmits 0x12 first then 0x34.

Exception response: server returns the original function code OR'd with 0x80 followed by a 1-byte exception code (1=Illegal Function, 2=Illegal Data Address, 3=Illegal Data Value, 4=Server Device Failure, 5=Acknowledge, 6=Server Device Busy, 8=Memory Parity Error, 0x0A=Gateway Path Unavailable, 0x0B=Gateway Target Device Failed to Respond).
PDU maximum size = 253 bytes (derived from 256-byte RS-485 ADU limit minus 1-byte address minus 2-byte CRC).
ADU maximum size: RTU/ASCII = 256 bytes; ASCII on the wire = 513 chars; TCP = 260 bytes (253 PDU + 7 MBAP).
Read Coils / Read Discrete Inputs (FC 1, 2) — up to 2000 (0x7D0) bits per request; coils packed 8 per byte LSB-first.
Read Holding / Read Input Registers (FC 3, 4) — up to 125 (0x7D) registers per request; each register is 2 bytes high-byte-first.
Write Single Coil (FC 5) — output value 0xFF00 = ON, 0x0000 = OFF; all other values illegal.
Write Multiple Coils (FC 15 / 0x0F) — up to 1968 (0x7B0) coils per request.
Write Multiple Registers (FC 16 / 0x10) — up to 123 (0x7B) registers per request.
Read/Write Multiple Registers (FC 23 / 0x17) — read up to 125 + write up to 121 registers in one transaction.
Mask Write Register (FC 22 / 0x16) — atomically modifies bits in a Holding Register using AND-mask + OR-mask: Result = (Current AND AND_Mask) OR (OR_Mask AND (NOT AND_Mask)).
Read FIFO Queue (FC 24 / 0x18) — drains up to 31 (0x1F) 16-bit registers from a FIFO at a specified pointer address.

File Record access (FC 20 / 0x14 Read, FC 21 / 0x15 Write) — accesses a Reference Type 6 file model; one record = up to 10000 registers per file; subgroups of records identified by File Number + Record Number + Record Length.

Serial-only Diagnostics: Read Exception Status (FC 7), Diagnostics (FC 8) with sub-functions 0..18 + 20, Get Comm Event Counter (FC 11 / 0x0B), Get Comm Event Log (FC 12 / 0x0C), Report Server/Slave ID (FC 17 / 0x11).

Encapsulated Interface Transport (FC 43 / 0x2B) carries an MEI Type field — MEI Type 13 (0x0D) = CANopen General Reference, MEI Type 14 (0x0E) = Read Device Identification (vendor / product / revision / etc.).

Three Function-Code Categories defined by Modbus.org: Public (1..64, 73..99, 111..127 — well-defined, unique, validated, publicly documented, with conformance tests), User-Defined (65..72 and 100..110 — implementer-chosen, not guaranteed unique), and Reserved (used by some companies for legacy products).
Reserved sub-codes within FC 8 (Diagnostics) are listed in Annex A. Function Code 43 with MEI Type 13 / 14 are the currently-published Encapsulated Interface Transports.
transaction_summary: A client builds the request ADU = optional-address + Function Code + Data + optional-CRC/LRC, sends it to the server. The server validates the function code (else exception 0x01), validates the data address (else 0x02), validates the data value (else 0x03), executes the function (else 0x04), and replies — either a normal response (echoes the function code with response data) or an exception response (function code | 0x80 + exception code).
data_model_summary: Discrete Inputs   : 1-bit RO, provided by an I/O system (e.g. physical input lines).
Coils             : 1-bit R/W, alterable by application program (e.g. physical output relay drives).
Input Registers   : 16-bit RO, provided by an I/O system (e.g. ADC conversions).
Holding Registers : 16-bit R/W, alterable by application program (e.g. set-points).
overview: MODBUS is the industry's serial de-facto standard since 1979. Originally invented by Modicon for its PLC family, it is now overseen by Modbus.org and exists as three open variants: Modbus RTU (binary, with CRC-16, on RS-232 or RS-485), Modbus ASCII (ASCII-hex, with LRC, line-readable), and Modbus TCP (binary PDU with a 7-byte MBAP header, on TCP/IP port 502). The application protocol is simple: a single-byte function code names an action (read coils, write a register, run diagnostics, etc.) and is followed by a function-code-dependent data field. Four memory-mapped tables — Discrete Inputs (1-bit RO), Coils (1-bit R/W), Input Registers (16-bit RO), and Holding Registers (16-bit R/W) — hold the device data. The protocol defines a clean exception mechanism: the server replies with the original function code OR'd with 0x80 followed by a 1-byte exception code naming the error (illegal function, illegal data address, illegal data value, device failure, acknowledge, busy, memory parity error, gateway path unavailable, gateway target failed). Because the application protocol is transport-agnostic, the same MODBUS PDU appears on a 1200-baud RS-485 line and on a 1 Gb/s switched-Ethernet TCP/IP segment.
block_diagram_components: MODBUS application layer (function-code processor) — common across all transports
Modbus RTU framer (ADU = Address + PDU + CRC-16; T3.5 silent-line end-of-frame detection)
Modbus ASCII framer (ADU = ':' + 2-ASCII-hex address + 2N-char PDU + LRC + CR LF)
Modbus TCP framer (MBAP Header: Transaction ID + Protocol ID = 0 + Length + Unit ID, on TCP socket port 502)
Four data tables: Discrete Inputs (1-bit RO), Coils (1-bit R/W), Input Registers (16-bit RO), Holding Registers (16-bit R/W)
Encapsulated Interface Transport (FC 43, MEI types 13 CANopen / 14 Read Device Identification)
process_technology: Not applicable — MODBUS is a published protocol specification (PDF), not a silicon part. Implementations exist as RTL IP cores, microcontroller firmware, PLC engines, embedded gateways, and software stacks (libmodbus, pymodbus, FreeModbus, etc.).
use_cases: Industrial PLC ↔ I/O device communication (read sensor inputs, write actuator outputs)
SCADA / HMI ↔ field-device polling over RS-485 multi-drop bus
Modbus TCP gateway bridging an Ethernet-side SCADA system to legacy serial Modbus RTU sub-networks
Building automation, HVAC, energy metering, and electric-utility substation telemetry
Renewable energy: inverter / battery-management-system data acquisition
Process control: chemical / oil-gas / water-treatment plant device polling
Variable-frequency drive (VFD) configuration and run-time monitoring
